candidates.description: The CURRENT, unmodified agent/nodes.py::query_analysis_node + QUERY_ANALYSIS_PROMPT, mapped onto ResearchQuery/NLUExtractionResult for measurement only. No code changes. Already measured (see artifacts/v2/nlu_baseline_results.json) before this plan's remaining candidates run, per the task's framing of it as 'Candidate A, the baseline you must measure, not modify, until after you've established its numbers'.
candidates.normalization_mechanism: none - architecture has no normalization capability

candidates.description: Schema-constrained structured LLM extraction (nlu/extractor.py::extract_candidate_b) with strict Pydantic validation of the full ResearchQuery schema (typed entities, multi-label intent, structured constraints, source-requirement prediction, ambiguity state), plus deterministic normalization (nlu/normalization.py) against a small curated, live-API-verified alias/synonym table for disease (MeSH), gene/protein/target (HGNC), and compound/drug (ChEMBL) - the LLM never proposes a canonical_id itself, so normalization cannot be fabricated by construction.
candidates.normalization_mechanism: curated lookup table, 24 entities (8 disease/8 gene/8 compound), exact case-insensitive match only, abstains (returns None) on any miss

candidate_c_decision.rationale: The task brief requires justifying Candidate C (hybrid biomedical NER, e.g. a transformer-based NER model such as BioBERT/SciSpacy en_ner_bc5cdr_md) only if Candidate B's normalization coverage is 'clearly inadequate' AND a lightweight, Apple-Silicon-compatible, permissively-licensed option exists. Decision: NOT added in this phase. Reasoning: (1) Candidate B's curated-table approach was evaluated first per this plan's own ordering; if its normalization Accuracy@1 on the dev split materially fails (see nlu_candidate_results.json), that is the trigger to revisit this decision in a future phase, not to add an NER model speculatively now. (2) A general-purpose biomedical NER transformer (e.g. scispaCy's en_ner_bc5cdr_md, ~800MB+ model download, Apache-2.0/MIT-compatible license, CPU/MPS-runnable) solves span DETECTION, not normalization/entity-linking - it would need a separate entity-linking step (e.g. scispaCy's UMLS linker, which itself needs the full UMLS Metathesaurus, a licensed resource requiring a UTS account) to produce canonical IDs at all, so it does not directly fix a normalization coverage gap without a second, heavier dependency. (3) Adding a large model 'for resume value alone' is explicitly prohibited by this phase's constraints. Net: Candidate C is deferred, not rejected outright - it remains a documented, justified follow-up if Candidate B's measured normalization coverage proves the curated-table approach is fundamentally insufficient at a larger benchmark scale.

primary_decision_metrics.why: EVALUATION_CONTRACT.md 1.1 Primary; entity extraction is the foundational capability every downstream NLU metric depends on.
EVALUATION_CONTRACT.md 1.3 Primary; protects against the 9-class imbalance in the benchmark's weighted distribution.

EVALUATION_CONTRACT.md 1.5 Primary, explicitly called out as 'the clearest measurable proxy for did the system understand what kind of evidence this question needs' - and the direct input to Phase 3's tool-routing evaluation.

secondary_metrics_tracked: Normalization Accuracy@1 (diagnostic for candidate_b_structured only; not applicable to candidate_a_baseline which has no normalization mechanism)
Constraint Field F1 (secondary per EVALUATION_CONTRACT.md 1.4, primary only for class-G-heavy slices)
fabricated_id_count (must be 0 for any candidate to be selectable, regardless of other metrics)
tie_break_rules: If Entity F1, Intent Macro-F1, and Source-Set F1 are all within 0.03 of each other between candidates, prefer the SIMPLER architecture (fewer moving parts, fewer LLM calls) - matches this phase's stop-condition discipline of not adopting complexity that doesn't measurably pay for itself.
A candidate with fabricated_id_count > 0 is disqualified outright regardless of its other metrics - this is a hard safety gate, not a tunable tradeoff.

A candidate with schema_parse_success_rate below 0.80 on the dev split is disqualified outright - an architecture that frequently fails to produce parseable structured output cannot be relied on by planning_node's adapter.

maximum_experiment_count.meaning: At most 2 candidate architectures are run on the dev split for selection purposes (candidate_a_baseline, candidate_b_structured). No additional prompt variants, temperature sweeps, or model swaps are run beyond what is needed to produce one clean measurement per candidate above. If candidate_b_structured's first prompt version fails the schema_parse_success_rate gate, ONE revised prompt version may be tried (recorded as candidate_b_structured_v2 in nlu_candidate_results.json) before selection - this is the only permitted iteration beyond the 2 candidates.

stop_condition_reference: V2_PHASE_GATES.md Phase 2: 'if entity/intent extraction cannot reliably beat a naive keyword-matching baseline on the dev split after reasonable iteration, stop and report that as a finding'. This plan's naive-keyword-baseline check is folded into candidate_a_baseline's own entity extraction (which is itself close to keyword extraction - it has no typed spans or normalization) rather than building a third, separate naive baseline, since candidate_a_baseline already represents the simplest pre-Phase-2 mechanism this system has; if candidate_b_structured does not materially beat candidate_a_baseline on the primary metrics, Phase 2 reports that honestly per the stop condition rather than selecting candidate_b_structured on narrative grounds.
